independence_declaration.statement: I (code-security-reviewer) authored no implementation in the reviewed scope (tools/gates, tools/agents, tools/source, CI workflow, agent definitions, analysis). My only writes are this record, its sidecars and my evidence under docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/code-security/round-19/. I formed this verdict without reading any other round-19 review record.

checks_run.procedure: Confirm the frozen candidate before reviewing
checks_run.command: git rev-parse HEAD; node tools/gates/candidate.mjs --stage DG0; git diff --stat 0a652018..HEAD
checks_run.environment: repository working tree, agent shell sandbox
checks_run.expected: candidate.mjs prints sha256:6720ad2c…922a; commits after the freeze touch only metadata
checks_run.actual: HEAD 3ffb28c (freeze/assignment commit). The working-tree candidate is sha256:6720ad2c5ea1d5bddb27a430536d27a962ded8224a373db101891e81d652922a (91 files). 0a65201..HEAD changes only assignments, the candidate manifest and stages.json. A fresh clone at 0a652018 also recomputes the same ID (--ref HEAD).

checks_run.procedure: Run the gate and agent test suites in a fresh disposable clone of the candidate commit
checks_run.command: git clone /home/user/My-owns $TMPDIR/dg0-sec; git checkout 0a652018; GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null node --test tools/gates/tests/*.test.mjs tools/agents/tests/*.test.mjs
checks_run.environment: fresh clone under $TMPDIR, node, bubblewrap available (nested)
checks_run.expected: all tests pass, none skipped; the F-DG0-152 case exercises both the control and the Landlock branch
checks_run.actual: 93 tests, 93 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped. F-DG0-152 diagnostics: without Landlock, viaProcRoot/viaProcCwd/viaProcRootTmp WROTE and the signal was allowed; with Landlock, all refused, own areas WROTE, nested bwrap works.

checks_run.procedure: Run the pre-freeze in a fresh clone of the candidate commit
checks_run.environment: fresh clone $TMPDIR/dg0-sec at 0a652018, sandboxed checks via sandbox-run.sh
checks_run.expected: all pre-freeze checks PASS; the working-tree candidate equals HEAD
checks_run.actual: All checks PASS (source extraction reproducible, validator and guard tests, runner tests, register rules, register merge, pipeline, 4 analysis checks); the working-tree candidate equals HEAD sha256:6720ad2c…922a

checks_run.procedure: Code review of the round-18→19 diff (landlock_exec.py, agent_sandbox.py, rules.mjs, import-findings.mjs, tests, threat-model, settings)
checks_run.expected: the changes implement D-033/D-034/D-035 without weakening other controls
checks_run.actual: landlock_exec.py is fail-closed and correct (ABI-6 scoped attr, no_new_privs, restrict_self before execv). The validator requires the landlock block. import-findings now skips record-less verifications instead of throwing (fail-safe: findings stay pending). The D-035 tolerance also covers the gate round (F-DG0-155). New project allow rules for git push/filter-branch/update-ref reach agents (F-DG0-156). The CI workflow is unchanged (pinned actions, fetch-depth 0).

checks_run.procedure: Verify F-DG0-152 on the live run: can this run reach a process outside its Landlock domain through /proc/<pid>/root
checks_run.environment: this agent run's shell (inside the process sandbox and Landlock domain)

checks_run.procedure: D-034: verify that the rewritten history is sound (write-once, restored blobs, no other change, nothing deleted)
checks_run.command: checkWriteOnce(DG0) in a fresh clone at 3ffb28c; git ls-tree HEAD reviews/DG0/round-17; pairwise git diff of backup/pre-writeonce-repair-565ab3f (89 commits) against rewritten ee4ddd7^ (89 commits); git log --diff-filter=D on reviews/runs/candidates
checks_run.environment: fresh clone and host repository (read-only git)
checks_run.expected: 0 write-once errors; blobs 862693f/276e32c; only the two restored adds differ; no deletes
checks_run.actual: 0 errors. Both files are at 862693f98291… and 276e32c201e2…, first added in their original round-17 auto-commit e9a00fd. All 89 commit pairs are identical apart from those two adds, with the same subjects. 0 delete events.

checks_run.procedure: D-035: reproduce the missing-source_commit tolerance for superseded rounds and for the gate round
checks_run.environment: disposable clone at 3ffb28c (manifest edited only in the clone, then restored)
checks_run.expected: the tolerance is limited to non-gate rounds; a gate with a non-existent source_commit is rejected
checks_run.actual: A1: findManifest accepts a non-existent source_commit on the gate-round manifest (0 errors). B: checkCandidate in current mode accepts it (0 errors). C: historical mode rejects it. A2: a reachable but wrong commit is still rejected. D-035 is acceptable for superseded rounds; its extension to the gate round is F-DG0-155 (Low).

checks_run.procedure: Residual 7 / F-DG0-149: read-only assessment of /proc exposure (mount configuration, namespaces, mode bits; no /proc/sys write)
checks_run.command: grep agent_sandbox.py bwrap args; awk mountinfo /proc; readlink /proc/self/ns/*; test -w /proc/sys/kernel/hostname
checks_run.environment: repository and this run's shell layer
checks_run.expected: the scope matches threat-model residual 7 (own-run; /proc/sys read-only for the shell)
checks_run.actual: Only an IPC namespace is created and the host procfs is bound read-write, so the reachable tunables are host-global, not own-run. The shell layer's topmost /proc mount is rw in the initial UTS namespace, and access(2) reports it writable. The residual is larger than stated (F-DG0-154, Medium).

checks_run.procedure: Whether the shell layer actually refuses /proc/sys writes (the threat model's 'read-only for the agent's shell' claim)
checks_run.command: not run: requires an actual /proc/sys write, which the assignment forbids
checks_run.actual: Not executed. The only non-write evidence (mount flags, access(2)) does not support the claim.

checks_run.procedure: Secrets scan of the candidate files and of the transcripts committed since round 18
checks_run.command: grep -rnIiE credential patterns over git ls-tree 0a652018 (excluding trading_agent, gz, docx); zcat of every .gz changed in 701870e9..3ffb28c | grep -cE 'sk-ant-…|ghp_…|AKIA…|BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY'
checks_run.actual: only regex text inside earlier evidence logs matched; 0 credential-pattern hits in the new transcripts

checks_run.procedure: Re-confirm the earlier fixes F-DG0-147/148/150/151/153 in code
checks_run.command: sed/grep agent_sandbox.py (docstring, --unshare-ipc, FileExistsError branch, accept pattern) and threat-model.md row 1
checks_run.actual: Present. F-DG0-153 is fixed (row 1 now says the PID namespace is shared and the IPC namespace is unshared). F-DG0-147 is still round-unpinned but fail-closed (re-accepted as an observation).

checks_run.procedure: CI workflow check: pinned actions, fetch-depth, whether it changed since round 18
checks_run.expected: least-privilege permissions, SHA-pinned actions, fetch-depth 0, unchanged
checks_run.actual: permissions block present, actions pinned to SHAs, fetch-depth 0; no change since round 18

summary: FAIL on one Medium finding. D-033 (per-run Landlock domain) is verified and F-DG0-152 closes, as does F-DG0-153. The D-034 history repair is sound. D-035 is acceptable for superseded rounds but also covers the gate round (F-DG0-155, Low). Threat-model residual 7 misstates its scope: the /proc/sys tunables are host-global, not own-run, and the shell-layer read-only claim is unsupported (F-DG0-154, Medium), so F-DG0-149 stays OPEN. Project allow rules for git push/filter-branch reach agents but are contained (F-DG0-156, Low). Tests 93/93 and the pre-freeze pass.
